title: Tetradecanuclearity in 3d–4f chemistry: relaxation and magnetocaloric effects in [NiII6LnIII8] species

material_class.structural_family: tetradecanuclear [Ni6Ln8] cluster; Ni6 octahedron encapsulating a Gd4 rhombus with two face-capping and two edge-capping Gd ions

synthesis.procedure: Under aerobic conditions, Ni(ClO4)2·6H2O (110 mg, 0.3 mmol), Gd(NO3)3·6H2O (135 mg, 0.3 mmol), 2-hydroxy-1-naphthaldehyde (52 mg, 0.3 mmol), 2-aminoisobutyric acid (31 mg, 0.3 mmol) and NEt3 were dissolved in MeOH/MeCN (10 mL, 1:1) to give a green solution. The solution was transferred to a 25 mL Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave and heated at 120 °C for 12 h. Slow cooling to room temperature gave light-green crystals of [Ni6Gd8(OH)10(L)6(aib)4(naphth)4(NO3)4(MeO)2]·MeCN·H2O in about 25–30% yield. The main text states the same solvothermal route with equimolar Ln(NO3)3·5H2O, Ni(ClO4)2·6H2O, Hnaphth, Haib and NEt3 in MeOH/MeCN (1:1) at 120 °C for ~12 h, but gives no reagent masses or molar amounts. SI elemental analysis for 1·MeCN·H2O: calcd (found) C 38.74 (38.59), H 3.36 (3.59), N 4.4 (4.53)%.
synthesis.vessel_or_method: 25 mL Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave, solvothermal, aerobic
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Slow cooling to room temperature afforded light-green crystals.

properties.summary: Dc susceptibility (0.1 T) gives χMT = 67.41 cm3 mol−1 K at room temperature, close to 67.45 cm3 mol−1 K for four NiII (g = 2.10) and eight non-interacting GdIII (g = 2.00); χMT stays nearly constant to ~25 K and rises to 88.5 cm3 mol−1 K at 5 K. The topology was not fitted. Heat capacity is strongly field-dependent below ~10 K, and the full spin entropy is calculated as Sm/R = 21.0 for four S = 1 NiII and eight S = 7/2 GdIII, but correlations prevent that value at low temperature. For ΔB = 0–7 T, −ΔSm reaches 14.2 R = 25.8 J kg−1 K−1 at 2.7 K, with maximum ΔTad = 8.6 K, so 1 is a Ni–Gd molecular magnetic refrigerant. No optical properties are reported.

synthesis.procedure: The same aerobic solvothermal procedure as for 1 was used, replacing Gd(NO3)3·6H2O with Dy(NO3)3·6H2O (135 mg, 0.3 mmol). Ni(ClO4)2·6H2O (110 mg, 0.3 mmol), 2-hydroxy-1-naphthaldehyde (52 mg, 0.3 mmol), 2-aminoisobutyric acid (31 mg, 0.3 mmol) and NEt3 in MeOH/MeCN (10 mL, 1:1) were heated in a 25 mL Teflon-lined autoclave at 120 °C for 12 h. Slow cooling gave light-green crystals of [Ni6Dy8(OH)10(L)6(aib)4(naphth)4(NO3)4(MeO)2]·MeCN·0.5H2O in about 25–30% yield. The main text gives the shared route and yield but no numerical reagent amounts. SI elemental analysis listed for 2·MeCN: calcd (found) C 38.81 (38.89), H 3.32 (3.91), N 4.41 (4.33)%.

properties.summary: Room-temperature χMT is 116.41 cm3 mol−1 K, close to 117.17 cm3 mol−1 K for four NiII (g = 2.10) and eight DyIII (S = 5/2, L = 5, J = 15/2, gJ = 4/3). On cooling, χMT falls to 105.02 cm3 mol−1 K near 16 K, then rises to 111.57 cm3 mol−1 K at 5 K (0.1 T). Ac data in a 3.5 G field (200–1000 Hz, 1.8–10 K) show in-phase intensity increasing on cooling and frequency- and temperature-dependent, not fully formed out-of-phase signals below ~5 K, indicating possible SMM behaviour. No optical properties or extracted energy barrier are reported.
